item.title: Annie-Claude joins the professoriate
item.description:
Université Laval welcomed Annie-Claude Laurin as a professeure assistante in its Faculté des sciences infirmières on 27 August 2025.

The announcement describes her intensive-care nursing experience and her research on ethics, epistemic injustice and nurses’ moral agency, including the political and philosophical dimensions of advanced nursing practice.

Read Laval’s appointment announcement, or meet Annie-Claude and explore her work with the collective.

item.title: Compost at IPONS 2026
item.description:
The 28th International Nursing Philosophy Conference met at UC Irvine and online on 22–24 July 2026. Its theme was Listening and Speaking Otherwise: Encounters at the Edge of Nursing and Philosophy. Jess co-chaired with Miriam Bender.

Seven members were represented on the programme. Jane facilitated Nursing the Borderlands, with Annie-Claude, Brandon and Eva. Jamie and Jess held the invited conversation Camp and the Politics of Seriousness in Nursing and Health Philosophy. Jamie also facilitated Camp, Professionalism, and Performative Critique, which included Abstractification in nursing education, co-authored by Tue-Chieu Mai and Patrick. Jamie joined Thinking the Event of Nursing. Jess facilitated Nursing Crip Futures.

item.title: Funding for LGBTQ2S+ nursing research
item.description:
On 5 February 2025, Université Laval announced a grant of CAD $14,000 from the Fondation de l’Institut universitaire de cardiologie et de pneumologie de Québec for Patrick Martin’s research.

The project explores the experiences of LGBTQ2S+ nurses caring for LGBTQ2S+ patients. It brings questions of care, sexuality and gender into nursing research.

Read Laval’s funding announcement, or meet Patrick and find his writing on care ethics and nurse resistance.
